summary: The Indoor Mapping Data Format is a community standard of the Open Geospatial Consortium, developed outside the consortium and published with Apple as copyright holder alongside it, that describes the inside of a venue such as an airport, shopping centre or train station. A delivery is a zip archive holding a manifest and one GeoJSON file per kind of feature: venues, buildings, floors, rooms, openings, fixtures, amenities, businesses, postal addresses, restricted zones and the links between rooms. It covers interior place description well, in global latitude and longitude, with a stated extension mechanism and a downloadable set of validation rules. It leaves meshes, materials, drawing and styling, device positioning, live data, identity and commerce to others. Traps for a standards audience: the data is flat and two-dimensional with floors stacked by an integer ordinal rather than by height, its curated paths are hints and not a routing network, the extension rules do not say what a reader without an extension should do, and the venue-type guidance pages are Apple advice outside the official standard.

coverage.note: IMDF models the rooms and entrances of a venue, not human or character bodies.

coverage.note: IMDF has a declared extension mechanism: identifiers with provider, name and version are listed in the Manifest, and extensions add feature types, members and validations without changing existing meaning. It gives no rule for a reader that does not know an extension, and it says it does not address clashes between extensions. GeoJSON itself defines no processing model for the foreign members this relies on.

coverage.note: An IMDF Anchor is a curated point from which a business record (an Occupant) takes its place in a room, and feature identifiers must be kept across deliveries, so such content stays tied to a place across sessions and readers. coverage.note: IMDF is a data model for interior spaces: venues, buildings, levels, units, openings, fixtures and amenities. It is a community standard of the Open Geospatial Consortium that was developed outside the consortium, with Apple named as copyright holder alongside it.

coverage.note: An IMDF archive declares itself through a Manifest with a creation time and keeps feature identifiers across deliveries, and features may carry start, end and modified times. The Manifest version field is the version of IMDF, not of the map, and there is no transform that aligns the map to another map of the place.

coverage.note: Every IMDF archive has one Venue polygon, and all other features must lie inside it, so the archive declares the area it covers in the GeoJSON frame. The polygon should be a formal property boundary or a reasonable pedestrian extent.

sources.quote: ALL other features MUST be within the polygonal boundary of the Venue

coverage.note: IMDF has identified zones (Geofence features with ids, categories, restrictions and parent links) that attribute the features inside them. It defines no events scoped to a zone and no summaries.

coverage.note: IMDF Openings model real doors and thresholds: a line whose length approximates the entrance width, a door type with an automatic flag, and a directed Relationship that gives one-way travel. It shows nothing of what lies beyond, and these are physical entrances, not links between worlds.
